entries.name: Spiritcaller
entries: Spiritcallers are a new phenomena in Prosperra. People born with an innate connection to the spirit world aren't anything new but since the departure of Veles, spirits no longer find their way to Zendan and the beyond. This has led to the development of a new kind of magic, powered by the spirits wandering Prosperra. Rather than drawing magic from the spirits into themselves, Spiritcallers convince spirits to aid them or their companions by bonding them for a short time.

A Spiritcaller can also sever this connection, using some of the binding energy to cast a spell. In contrast to Wraithwielders, Spiritcallers are more on the fringes of society as messing with spirits is seen as a dangerous practice that disrupts the natural order between the living and the dead. As they struggle to find acceptance, Spiritcallers have begun to follow different paths, specializing in the many ways their bond with spirits can be used.

classFeature.name: Spirit Bonds
entries: Your connection to the spirits allows you to request their aid, establishing temporary bonds that provide benefits.

When you finish a Long Rest, you select Spirits from the table below equal to your proficiency bonus. Each type of spirit grants a benefit that scales with your Spiritcaller level, see the Spirit Magic table above.

You assign them to yourself or to a willing member of your adventuring party. A person can be bonded to only one Spirit at a time, the bond lasting until their next Long rest, unless prematurely severed by the Spiritcaller

classFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: You have learned to channel the magical energy that is released upon severing the spirit bond into spells.

Certain spirits embody particular types of magical energy, and the process to learn how to attract a specific type of spirit and cast a spell from its energy requires considerable knowledge and practice.
As you gain experience, you can attract increasingly more potent spirits which can be used to cast more powerful spells.

entries.name: Bond Spells
entries: Rather than preparing spells normally, you select your Spirit bonds after every Long Rest. Each bond is associated with a type of magic and severing the bond allows you to cast a spell of that school of magic from the Spiritcaller spell list if the spell is of a level equal to or lower than the level of the spirit.
The amount of spirit bonds you can form is shown in the Spiritcaller Spirit magic table.

entries.name: Types of Spirits known
entries: As a Spiritcaller you start by knowing how to attract 1 type of spirit from among the types listed in the Spirit Types Table. You learn additional types of spirits at level 5, 9, 13 and 17 but you cannot select subclass specific spirits.

entries.name: Breaking the Bond
entries: As a Magic action, you can sever one of your active Spirit bonds. The bonded person must be within 30 feet of you, and you must be able to see them. You can also sever a bond you bear yourself.

When you sever a bond, its passive benefit immediately ends. You can then cast one spell from your spell list that belongs to the school of magic associated with that Spirit. The spell must be of a level equal to or lower than the level of the Spirit, as shown in the Spirit table.
The spell requires no spell slot. If the spell is of a lower level than the Spirit, the spell takes on the Spirit's level for that casting, as if you had used a spell slot of that level.
You otherwise follow the normal rules for casting the spell, including its components, concentration, targets, and duration.
If the spell has a casting time of a Bonus Action, you can take a Bonus Action to sever the bond and cast the spell instead.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Spiritcaller spells.

You use your Intelligence whenever a Spiritcaller spell refers to your spellcasting ability. You also use your Intelligence modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a Spiritcaller spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.
Spell save DC = 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Intelligence modifier
Spell attack modifier = your Proficiency Bonus + your Intelligence modifier

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use an arcane focus, a spiritual focus, or a weapon with which you have proficiency as a Spellcasting Focus for your Spiritcaller spells.

classFeature.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: Your training with weapons allows you to use the Mastery properties of two kinds of weapons with which you have proficiency such as a Light crossbow or a Pistol.
Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose.

classFeature.name: Fighting Style
entries: You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice for which you qualify.
You can't choose the same Fighting Style more than once, even if you later gain another Fighting Style feature.

classFeature.name: Soul Mark
entries: Your understanding of the spiritual energy inside the living allows you to mark the souls of those you harm.
When you deal damage to a creature with an attack that exceeds 8 + their Charisma modifier, you mark that creature's soul at the end of your turn.
The mark remains until it is removed by this feature or the target has taken a long rest.
Each time you deal damage to a creature whose soul is marked, the mark's intensity increases by 1.

items: Soulrend: As a Bonus Action, you can rend the soul of a creature within 30 ft that you have marked. The mark ends, and the creature takes 2d6 Psychic damage for each point of the mark's intensity. The creature can't take Reactions until the end of its next turn.

At Higher Levels. Your Soulrend damage die changes when you reach certain Spiritcaller levels, as shown in the Souldrend Die column of the Spiritcaller Features table. The die becomes a d8 at level 6, a d10 at level 11, and a d12 at level 16.

classFeature.name: Spiritcaller Subclass
entries: You gain a Spiritcaller Subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Spiritcaller levels.
For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Spiritcaller level or lower.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat for which you qualify.
You gain this feature again at 8th, 12th, and 16th level.

classFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

classFeature.name: Binding Presence
entries: When a creature dies within 30 feet of you, you're able to keep the spirit tethered to its body.
You can can ask the spirit associated with the body one question. It's under no obligation to be truthful, and it answers as concisely as possible, eager to leave its body behind.

The spirit knows only what it knew in life, as determined by the DM. Each additional question asked while the spirit remains tethered has a 30% chance of causing the Spirit to transform into a Wraith; roll on the Wraith's Revenge table when this transformation occurs.

classFeature.name: Resonating Rend
entries: When you use Soulrend, the spiritual wounds you inflict resonate between those you rend. You roll one additional Soulrend damage die for each creature you rend beyond the first.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat for which you qualify.
You gain this feature again at 12th, and 16th level.

classFeature.name: Lingering Bond
entries: Your understanding of spiritual magic allows you to preserve a Spirit bond while drawing upon some of its power.
When you sever a Spirit bond to cast a spell, you can instead preserve the bond and cast a spell of that type that is of a lower level than the Spirit's level.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

classFeature.name: Spiritvision
entries: Your connection to the spirit world allows you to see the true spiritual energy of all living things.
As a Magic action, you gain Truesight with a range of 120 feet for 1 hour. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat for which you qualify.
You gain this feature again at 16th level.

classFeature.name: Spirit Bond Mastery
entries: Your bonds with the spirit world have become more flexible.
You can now assign multiple bonds to yourself or to a willing member of your adventuring party. Each of the bonds must be with a different type of spirit.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Improved Soulrend
entries: Your ability to rend a creature's spirit can disrupt its connection to the source of their magic.
When you use your Soulrend ability, the target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your Spiritcaller spell save DC or be unable to cast spells until the end of your next turn.
If you use Soulrend on the same target again, it gains a cumulative +2 bonus to the saving throw for each time this effect has affected it this combat.

classFeature.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Avatar of the Spirits
entries: You have become a living conduit between the material world and the spirit realm.
Whenever you roll Initiative, you can restore one Spirit bond that you previously severed during the current adventuring day.
The restored Bond returns to the creature that originally bore it, and its passive benefit immediately resumes.
Once you restore a Bond using this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Short Rest.
In addition, while you have at least one active Spirit bond, you gain a +2 bonus to your Intelligence score, to a maximum of 22.

classFeature.name: Bond Types Known
entries: Your Bonds are manifestations of the spirits you have learned to commune with.
A Spiritcaller does not automatically know every Gift. Your Spiritcaller level determines how many Gift types you know.
At the end of a Long Rest, you choose which known Gifts to assign.
Each Gift has exactly one associated spell.
Severing a Gift casts that Gift's associated spell at the highest Gift Spell Level you can use.

classFeature.name: Spiritcaller Subclass
entries: You gain a Spiritcaller Subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Spiritcaller levels.
For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Spiritcaller level or lower.

classFeature.name: Spiritcaller Subclass
entries: Your chosen Spiritcaller Subclass grants you a feature at this level.

subclassFeature.name: The Haunt Subclass
entries: A Haunt turns the fear and unease people have towards the spirits of the dead into a weapon, calling upon them to cause nightmares and illusions that prey upon the minds of their targets.
Some are hired to torment those who refuse the demands of the powerful, while others take justice into their own hands, haunting those who escaped judgment.
Whatever their cause, a Haunt knows that sometimes the fear of their victims in the afterlife is enough to make the guilty face what they have done.

subclassFeature.name: The Haunt Cantrips
entries: When you choose this Subclass, choose one Enchantment cantrip and one Illusion cantrip from the Spiritcaller spell list.
While you or another creature within 30 feet of you has a Spirit bond, you can cast those cantrips without severing a Spirit bond.
You can choose one additional cantrip from the Spiritcaller spell list at 8th, 12th, and 16th level. Each cantrip you choose with this feature must be an Enchantment or Illusion cantrip.

subclassFeature.name: Haunted Marks
entries: Your haunting magic that influences the minds of your foes also leaves a mark upon their souls.
When a creature fails a saving throw against an Enchantment or Illusion spell or cantrip you cast, you can mark its soul at the end of your turn.
If the spell or cantrip causes multiple creatures to fail their saving throws, choose one of those creatures to mark.

subclassFeature.name: Haunting Whispers
entries: As a Bonus Action, you can torment a creature marked by your Soul Mark, consuming the mark in the process. Choose one of the following effects and remove the Soul Mark on the target:

items: Dread: The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your Spiritcaller spell save DC or have the Frightened condition for 1 minute. The target repeats the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Delusion: The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your Spiritcaller spell save DC or it must use its next action on its turn to make a melee attack against a creature other than itself that you mentally choose. The target can act normally on its turn if you choose no creature or if no creature is within its reach.

entries: You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Soul Tracking
entries: Your connection to a creature's soul allows you to sense its presence even when it is beyond your sight. While a creature bears your Soul Mark, you know the direction and distance of the creature from you, provided you are on the same plane of existence.

subclassFeature.name: Twisted Reality
entries: Your mastery of the mind allows you to blur the boundary between reality and illusion, making your hauntings almost impossible to escape.

When a creature bearing your Soul Mark makes a saving throw against your Haunting Whispers feature, or against an Illusion or Enchantment spell or Cantrip you cast, it has Disadvantage on the saving throw.
While you are within 30 feet of a creature bearing your Soul Mark, you have Advantage on Constitution saving throws you make to maintain Concentration.
In addition your Haunting Whispers feature no longer consumes the Soul Mark when used.

subclassFeature.name: The Spectre Subclass
entries: A Spectre has learned to blur the boundary between the living and the dead.

Their connection to the spirit world allows them to bypass barriers and obstacles that would stop the living. Many Spectres are therefore hired as assassins, thieves, and spies, using their unnatural abilities to slip past guards and penetrate even the most secure locations.
Others turn their gifts toward less sinister pursuits, exploring forgotten ruins and places too dangerous for ordinary adventurers.
Whether they seek fortune, knowledge, or danger, a Spectre is never truly bound by the barriers of the mortal world.

subclassFeature.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: When you choose to become a Spectre at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with shields and martial weapons with the Finesse property.

subclassFeature.name: Spirit Stabs
entries: Your bonded spirit strikes alongside you.
While you are bonded to a Spirit, once per turn when you hit with a Melee attack, you can deal extra damage equal to your Intelligence modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Spiritual Armor
entries: Your bonded spirit can reinforce your body against harm.

While you are bonded to a Spirit, if you take damage from an attack or other damaging effect, you can take a Reaction to reduce the damage by an amount equal to your Intelligence modifier + your Proficiency Bonus.
You can use this Reaction a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Echo Step
entries: Your bonded spirit can briefly bring you from the Material Plane to the spirit world.
While you are bonded to a Spirit, as a Bonus Action, you teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Spectral Form
entries: You have learned to fully shed your physical form and become a spirit for a short time.

As a Bonus Action, you enter your Spectral Form for 1 minute. While in this form, you gain a Fly Speed equal to your Speed and have Resistance to nonmagical Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

While in Spectral Form, you can move through creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain. When you move through a creature, that creature takes Force damage equal to your Intelligence modifier. A creature can take this damage only once per turn.
If you end your turn inside a creature or an object, you take 5 Force damage and are moved to the nearest unoccupied space.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: The Soulmender Subclass
entries: A Soulmender understands the delicate bond between body and spirit.
Through strange rituals, forbidden medicine, and communion with spirits, they can mend what is broken, ward off death, and draw upon the powers of the dead to restore the living.

Many become doctors of last hope, called upon when doctors have failed and prayers have gone unanswered. A Soulmender's greatest gift is the ability to reconnect a wandering spirit with its body, defying a boundary that every other healer accepts as absolute.
While these practices may have made them an outcast in society nobles, who publicly condemn their methods, may secretly still send for a Soulmender when their beloved has died.
Still, a soul returned to its body may not always return unchanged, and most Soulmenders keep moving from place to place to avoid the consequences of their work.

subclassFeature.name: The Soulmender Cantrips
entries: When you choose this Subclass, choose one Enchantment cantrip and one Necromancy cantrip from the Spiritcaller spell list.
While you or another creature within 30 feet of you has a Spirit bond, you can cast those cantrips without severing a Spirit bond.
You can choose one additional cantrip from the Spiritcaller spell list at 8th, 12th, and 16th level. Each cantrip you choose with this feature must be a Necromancy or Enchantment cantrip.

subclassFeature.name: Soulbreaking Magic
entries: Your magic can now reach beyond the body, leaving its mark upon the soul of those you harm.

When you deal more damage then 8 + the target's Charisma modifier with a Necromancy or Enchantment cantrip or spell, you can mark that creature's soul as if you had dealt damage with an attack at the end of your turn.
If the cantrip or spell deals enough damage to multiple creatures, choose one of those creatures to mark.

subclassFeature.name: Soulkindling
entries: you have learned to use some of the spiritual energy from tethered spirits for your own uses.

When a creature you can see enters the space of one of the tethered spirits from your Binding Presence Feature, you can use your reaction to release the tether and choose one of the following effects:
Mending Magic: That creature regains hit points equal to 1d8 + your Intelligence modifier.
Harmful Magic: That creature gets a Soul Mark at the end of its turn.
You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Soulburst
entries: At 10th level, you can unleash the spiritual energy flowing through you in a devastating wave. As an action, you release a spirit energy explosion centered on yourself, extending in a 20-foot radius.
Each creature within the radius is affected according to its spiritual connection to you:
Bonded Spirits: A creature that is bonded to one of your spirits is flooded with restorative energy and regains 3d8 + your Spiritcaller level in hit points.

Soul Marked: A creature bearing your Soul Mark is struck by the explosion taking 6d8 necrotic damage. A creature can make a Constitution saving throw against your Spiritcaller spell save DC, taking half damage on a successful save and removing its Soul Mark
The explosion does not affect creatures that are neither bonded to one of your spirits nor marked by your Soul Mark. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Soulweaving
entries: You have learned to turn the spiritual energy of your Soulrend toward healing rather than destruction.

When you use your Soulrend feature, you can forgo its damage and instead restore Hit Points to one creature that is within 30 feet of you. The creature regains a number of Hit Points equal to the damage the Soulrend would have dealt.
You can use this benefit a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: The Haunt Spells
entries: Your spiritual discipline grants you additional spells. When you reach a Spiritcaller level specified in the The Haunt Spells table, you add the listed spells to your Spiritcaller spell list.

subclassFeature.name: The Spectre Spells
entries: Your connection to spirits grants you additional spells. When you reach a Spiritcaller level specified in the The Spectre Spells table, you add the listed spells to your Spiritcaller spell list.

subclassFeature.name: The Soulmender Spells
entries: Your spiritual bonds grant you additional spells. When you reach a Spiritcaller level specified in the The Soulmender Spells table, you add the listed spells to your Spiritcaller spell list.
